why: 2026 guidance: adjusted sales and operating profit **0% to −6% at CER** (raised in August from −4% to −12%). The basic model had +6.4%.

2027: the Medicare negotiated price for semaglutide (\$274 a month, 71% off list) takes effect, and the US list price drops to \$675. Novo says net price is unchanged, but most-favoured-nation clauses and Medicaid cuts are pressuring realized prices. Reviewed at −8%.

Semaglutide compound patents have already expired in some international markets, and US exclusivity runs to about 2031–32. Reviewed with dips in 2031–32 before oral Wegovy, CagriSema and amycretin carry growth.
GAAP operating margin falls from 41% to **32%** by 2035 (bear 27%, bull 37%) as price resets outpace volume.
2026 guidance: revenue **\$60.5–62.5B** (midpoint −1.7% vs. 2025). The basic model had +3.9%.

Analysts put about **\$17B** of revenue at risk from patent expiries through 2028–2030: Ibrance and Xtandi around 2027, Eliquis in 2028, part of the Prevnar franchise. Pfizer only says the impact accelerates from 2026 to 2030. Reviewed with declines of −4% / −9% / −3% in 2027–29, then recovery as Seagen ADCs, Metsera obesity assets and launches build.

Pfizer reports amortization, restructuring and other deductions below the cost lines. The XBRL-derived 2025 margin (36%) is therefore before about \$5B of amortization, and the reviewed target is **26%** (bear 21%, bull 30%).
Dividend yield is about 5.8% (\$1.72 a year), with an 89% cash payout ratio.
2026 guidance: turnover **+3–5%**, core operating profit +7–9%, reaffirmed with Q2.
Dolutegravir loses exclusivity **2028–2030**; it's the largest HIV franchise (about £2.1B a quarter). Reviewed at 0% / −2% in 2028–29, offset partly by long-acting cabotegravir.

GSK targets **more than £40B of sales by 2031** (about 3–4% a year) and a stable to improving margin through the patent cliff, helped by a £1.9B cost programme. Reviewed GAAP margin target **25%** (bear 20%, bull 30%) vs. a core margin above 31%.
2026 guidance raised to **about +10%** sales growth at CER (Q2 sales +17.8%, Dupixent +37.6%). The basic model had +6.2%.
Sanofi targets about **€25B of Dupixent** and €10B from launches by 2030. Dupixent's US exclusivity ends around 2031, so the review shows declines in 2031–32.
The 2025 GAAP margin (14.5%) includes impairments and amortization. Reviewed start 18% (3-year median), target **25%** (bear 20%, bull 30%); business operating margin runs near 30%.

2026 guidance cut in August: revenue **\$9.12–9.32B** (organic −3% to −1%) and adjusted EPS \$6.15–6.25, down from \$6.85–7.00. US revenue −7% on fewer vet visits and competition in dermatology and parasiticides. The basic model had +1.2%.
Librela plus its long-acting successor fell 8% in Q2. Reviewed with a recovery to +4–5% from 2028 as international growth (+6%) continues.
The EPS cut implies the margin drops to about **35%** in 2026 (from 39%); the reviewed target is 36% (bear 32%, bull 39%).
2026 guidance raised to **\$5.13–5.26B** of net product sales (Jakafi \$3.22–3.27B, Opzelura \$1.05–1.10B), plus royalties.

**Jakafi's US patent coverage ends in December 2028** (composition of matter plus pediatric exclusivity). Jakafi is over 60% of sales, so the review has revenue −28% in 2029 and −8% in 2030. The basic model grew it at 21%, fading.

Incyte targets **\$3–4B from the business excluding Jakafi by 2030**. The reviewed path reaches about \$4.1B of total revenue in 2030, and the margin target drops to **20%** (from 30%) after losing its highest-margin product.
2026 guidance raised to **\$1.835–1.910B** of revenue (royalties \$1.220–1.245B, adjusted EBITDA \$1.225–1.280B): about +34%. Darzalex SC and Vyvgart Hytrulo drive it.

ENHANZE royalties step down country by country when the rHuPH20 patents expire. Investors focus on **2027–2029**, and the 10-Q says Janssen's own Darzalex patents don't delay the step-down. Reviewed at −12% / −10% in 2029–30, then flat as MDASE and Hypercon deals build.
The GAAP margin was depressed by acquisition amortization (TTM 36%) while adjusted EBITDA runs at about 67%. Reviewed start 50%, target **45%** (bear 38%, bull 52%).

2026: Ingrezza guidance raised to **\$2.825–2.875B**, Crenessity \$184M in Q2 (about 15% of diagnosed CAH patients), and VYKAT XR from the Soleno deal (closed May 18, about \$94M a quarter pro forma). Total ≈ \$3.85B, +35%.

Ingrezza qualified for the small-biotech exception; it can be selected for Medicare negotiation from 2027, with the price applying in **2029**, and Teva's Austedo already has a negotiated price. Reviewed growth slows to +2% in 2029.
The margin target rises to **32%** (bear 26%, bull 38%) as Crenessity and VYKAT scale; the basic model used 23%.
SEC XBRL stops at FY2025 (March 2025), so the basic model projected +15% for FY2026. Actual FY2026 revenue was **₹33,593 crore, +3.2%**, with EBITDA 22.8% (24.7% adjusted).

Q1 FY2027 revenue was **−5.6%**: North America generics fell 41% as generic Revlimid fell away, and a ₹240 crore semaglutide API charge hit margins. Reviewed FY2027 at −3%, then +7% as India (+17%) and emerging markets carry growth.
The reviewed margin starts at 16% (FY2026, after one-offs) with a target of **19%** (bear 15%, bull 22%).
